scope: Independent read-only source and actual-signal regression-plan review before compiler gate. No build, GPU, runtime, UI or shared edit.

resolved_findings.issue: Finished interruption fell through into GPU repaint after exit request.
resolved_findings.resolution: Final proposal records completed result and returns immediately after exit for every non-retained completion. Interrupted returns before repaint as well. paint/resumed reject work once cancel is set.

resolved_findings.issue: Before-worker signal fixture initially did not force worker to stay active.
resolved_findings.resolution: Final fixture blocks worker on release_rx and releases it only after actual TERM is observed and production interrupt policy confirms no premature exit.

resolved_findings.issue: Initial signal tests bypassed production UI cancellation policy.
resolved_findings.resolution: Final subprocess tests directly exercise Startup::complete/interrupt methods used by user_event, together with actual Listener signal delivery. Display-specific dispatch remains an explicit runtime gate.

verified_properties: Listener is registered before graphical lifecycle worker and owned until after retained failure UI exits. Signal-safe machinery writes pending signal/pipe; normal reader stores cancellation before sending Update::Interrupted through winit EventLoopProxy.

Failure-complete then interrupt exits immediately with signal status. Interrupt while worker active only marks cancellation, leaving existing managed-child/group guards to perform cleanup; Finished then exits without retained failure UI or GPU repaint.
No timer/polling/frame wake is added. Existing ControlFlow::Wait remains. No new unsafe block or application Mutex is introduced.

Listener finish closes pipe and joins reader only outside run_app; close wakes idle forever iterator. Destructor only closes and never waits. Error paths do not retain an uncloseable helper; thread data remains owned if destructor detaches.

Legacy permanent atomic-only signal registrations are removed, avoiding duplicate registrations and preserving one scoped signal lifetime for graphical and headless launch paths. INT130/TERM143/HUP129 map remains.
Feature addition is signal-hook iterator/channel only, with no new package or lockfile changes. Startup dependency remains Unix guarded.

Actual TERM fixture uses unique environment token and identity-pinned process signaling, bounded readiness/delivery/exit checks, and direct-owned Child kill fallback only for test failure cleanup. After-worker arm reaps synthetic failing child and joins worker before announcing readiness. Before-worker arm is barrier-forced. Closed receiver and signal-free close both test reader lifetime.
notes: signal-hook internally uses a registration-list Mutex during setup/final teardown, as does its underlying registry. No such lock is used by the signal handler, normal cancellation delivery, rendering or native UI callback. Thus no new application/hot-path waiting lock is present; do not describe the dependency as literally containing no locks.

Current actual-process tests use channel delivery plus real Startup policy, not a winit application loop or managed game process group/installation lock. Existing owned-child cleanup tests remain unchanged. Fresh display-authorized actual launcher TERM-after-failure, active-child cleanup, lock release and unrelated-process survival checks remain required before runtime promotion.

Headless helper keeps previous worker result behavior; signal arriving after its worker has already returned does not get a retained UI to dismiss. This review qualifies the causal graphical lifetime fix, not a stronger cross-thread signal-ordering guarantee.
decision: No blocking source issue in stable proposal1. Ready for authorized isolated compiler and actual-signal CPU regression gates. Frozen f7b/audio PE remain untouched; no shipping/runtime acceptance.
